problem.paragraph: If $$f_{x}{({a,b})} = 0$$ and $$f_{y}{({a,b})} = 0$$ , then $$f$$ must have a relative extremum at $$({a,b})$$ .
If $$({a,b})$$ is a critical point of $$f$$ and both the conditions $$f_{\mathit{xx}}{({a,b})} < 0$$ and $$f_{\mathit{yy}}{({a,b})} < 0$$ hold, then $$f$$ has a relative maximum at $$({a,b})$$ .
If $$f{({x,y})}$$ has a relative maximum at $$({a,b})$$ , then $$f_{x}{({a,b})} = 0$$ and $$f_{y}{({a,b})} = 0$$ .
Let $$h{({x,y})} = f{(x)} + g{(y)}$$ . If $$f{(x)} > 0$$ and $$g{(y)} < 0$$ , then $$h$$ cannot have a relative maximum or a relative minimum at any point.

If $$f{({x,y})}$$ satisfies $$f_{\mathit{xx}}{({a,b})} \neq 0$$ , $$f_{\mathit{xy}}{({a,b})} = 0$$ , $$f_{\mathit{yy}}{({a,b})} \neq 0$$ , and $$f_{\mathit{xx}}{({a,b})} + f_{\mathit{yy}}{({a,b})} = 0$$ at the critical point $$({a,b})$$ of $$f$$ , then $$f$$ cannot have a relative extremum at $$({a,b})$$ .

Suppose $$h{({x,y})} = f{(x)} + g{(y)}$$ , where $$f$$ and $$g$$ have continuous second derivatives near $$a$$ and $$b$$ , respectively. If $$a$$ is a critical number of $$f$$ , $$b$$ is a critical number of $$g$$ , and $$f^{''}{(a)}g^{''}{(b)} > 0$$ , then $$h$$ has a relative extremum at $$({a,b})$$ .
If $$f_{\mathit{xx}}$$ and $$f_{\mathit{yy}}$$ have opposite signs at a critical point $$({a,b})$$ of $$f$$ , then $$f$$ has a saddle point at $$({a,b})$$ .
